Physical & Chemical Characteristics: This soil is the most widespread in the district, covering approximately 60% of the geographical area.
Locations (Taluks / Regions): Major concentrations are found in Palladam, Coimbatore, Mettupalayam, Pollachi, and Udumalpet taluks.
Agricultural Suitability and Productivit: Deep red calcareous variants in Pollachi and Udumalpet are highly suitable for intensive coconut plantation systems.

Physical & Chemical Characteristics: These are clay to clay loam soils with high shrink-swell properties that form wide cracks when dry, and have high water-holding capacity.
Locations (Taluks / Regions): Mainly occupies the highlands of the Coimbatore, Palladam, and Avinashi taluks.
Agricultural Suitability and Productivit: They possess ideal moisture-retention properties for cotton cultivation, though slow infiltration can sometimes cause waterlogging.

Physical & Chemical Characteristics: These soils feature deep, fertile loamy profiles that often exceed 30 meters in thickness.
Locations (Taluks / Regions): Confined to small patches along the Noyyal River and the Siruvani valley.
Agricultural Suitability and Productivit: They are highly fertile and support continuous, intensive crop production.

Physical & Chemical Characteristics: Composed predominantly of sand and gravel beds, or silt and kankar with admixtures of sand.
Locations (Taluks / Regions): Found primarily in the Chinnathadagam and Chitrachavadi sub-basins, and as scattered patches at the foothills of the Anaimalai range.
Agricultural Suitability and Productivit: Supports various cultivated crops and allows for groundwater development through shallow dug wells.

Physical & Chemical Characteristics: These soils possess a distinct surface layer rich in decomposing organic matter.
Locations (Taluks / Regions): Confined strictly to the reserve forest areas of the Western Ghats and the Valparai hilly area.
Agricultural Suitability and Productivit: Rich in organic content, making them highly suitable for plantation crops like tea, coffee, and spices.

Physical & Chemical Characteristics: Moderately shallow, well-drained, reddish-brown sandy loam soils with high bulk density and low water-holding capacity.
Locations (Taluks / Regions): It is the single largest soil series, occupying 2,15,405 hectares across the district.
Agricultural Suitability and Productivit: Categorized as having poor agricultural productivity and is prone to dense subsoil hard pan formation.

Physical & Chemical Characteristics: Moderately deep to deep, dark brown to dark reddish-brown sandy clay loam that is alkaline and highly calcareous.
Locations (Taluks / Regions): Occurs generally on very gentle slopes across the district plains.
Agricultural Suitability and Productivit: Categorized as having average productivity, but is well-suited for cultivating maize, groundnut, and pulses under irrigated conditions.

Physical & Chemical Characteristics: Very deep, calcareous, sandy clay loam to loamy sand soils with a moderate cation exchange capacity.
Locations (Taluks / Regions): Distributed on gentle slopes and urban zones in the district.
Agricultural Suitability and Productivit: Exhibits good productivity and is highly responsive to organic amendments like vermicompost and humic acid to improve nutrient retention.

Physical & Chemical Characteristics: Deep, fertile soils that benefit from surrounding geographical features.
Locations (Taluks / Regions): Located heavily around the Anamalais region, representing over 20% of the coconut land cover in the study area.
Agricultural Suitability and Productivit: Exhibits good yield potential and is one of the most productive soil series for extensive coconut farming.

Physical & Chemical Characteristics: Red soils that frequently develop a dense, compacted subsoil hard pan at a depth of 15-20 cm due to clay and calcium carbonate accumulation.
Locations (Taluks / Regions): Found extensively across the district, occupying roughly 1,22,965 hectares.
Agricultural Suitability and Productivit: Classified under poor productivity due to compaction, requiring physical interventions like chiseling to support deep-rooted crops.
